field_type_2026: Natural grass — hybrid Kentucky bluegrass reinforced with woven synthetic fibers, installed over a layered drainage/ventilation structure with grow lighting (replacing the venue's normal artificial turf); reversible after the tournament
iconic_games_note: SoFi Stadium opened in 2020 and has no prior men's World Cup history (2026 is its first). It is primarily an NFL venue, but has a short top-tier international football pedigree, clearly labelled here as non-World-Cup events: (1) 2023 CONCACAF Gold Cup Final, 16 Jul 2023 — Mexico 1-0 Panama (Santiago Gimenez 88'), att. 72,963, then the highest-attended football match at the stadium [VERIFIED: Wikipedia 2023 CONCACAF Gold Cup final + ESPN gameId 678990]; (2) 2024 CONMEBOL Copa America GROUP D, 24 Jun 2024 — Brazil 0-0 Costa Rica, att. 67,158 [CORRECTED from 'Group B' to 'Group D'; VERIFIED via Wikipedia 2024 Copa America, ESPN gameId 690712, CopaAmerica.com]; (3) 2024 CONMEBOL Copa America Group B, 26 Jun 2024 — Venezuela 1-0 Mexico (Salomon Rondon 57' pen.), att. 72,773 [VERIFIED: Wikipedia 2024 Copa America]. Major non-football events (clearly NON-football): Super Bowl LVI (13 Feb 2022, Rams 23-20 Bengals), 2023 College Football Playoff National Championship, WrestleMania 39 (2023); and the venue is set to host the 2028 Summer Olympics opening/closing ceremonies. The dedicated iconic_games list is intentionally left empty because these are tournament finals/group matches rather than historic men's World Cup lore.

renovations.change: Artificial turf removed and replaced with a natural-grass FIFA pitch: a hybrid Kentucky-bluegrass surface reinforced with woven synthetic fibers, grown over a layered structure with drainage, a vacuum-based ventilation layer, and grow lighting to sustain living grass inside the closed/canopied stadium. All modifications reversible to NFL configuration after the tournament.

city_history.founded: Inglewood incorporated 1908; Los Angeles founded 1781 (El Pueblo de Nuestra Senora la Reina de los Angeles)
city_history.significance: SoFi Stadium sits in Inglewood, California, in the Los Angeles metropolitan area roughly 4.8 km from Los Angeles International Airport, built on the former Hollywood Park Racetrack site as the anchor of the Hollywood Park mixed-use development. Greater Los Angeles is the second-largest U.S. metro and a global entertainment capital; the stadium is also slated to host ceremonies for the 2028 Summer Olympics.
city_history.football_culture: Los Angeles is one of the strongest soccer markets in the United States, anchored by a large Mexican-American and broader Latino population that gives CONCACAF and CONMEBOL fixtures near-home-crowd atmospheres (Mexico routinely sells out the LA area, as at the 2023 Gold Cup Final). The metro hosts two MLS clubs (LA Galaxy and LAFC) and a deep history of high-profile international matches at the Rose Bowl and now SoFi Stadium. Note: the football culture attaches to the Los Angeles metro, not the small city of Inglewood itself.

stadium_history_facts: Opened 8 September 2020 in Inglewood, California, on the former Hollywood Park Racetrack site within the Hollywood Park development.
Designed by HKS, Inc.; total cost estimated at roughly $5.5 billion by May 2020, making it among the most expensive stadiums ever built.
Home to two NFL franchises, the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers, both since 2020.
Owned by StadCo LA / Hollywood Park Land Company (Rams owner Stan Kroenke).
Roofed by a freestanding translucent ETFE canopy spanning about one million square feet (302 panels) and features the dual-sided oval 4K 'Infinity Screen' video board.
Hosted Super Bowl LVI in February 2022 (Rams 23-20 Bengals) and the 2023 College Football Playoff National Championship.
Hosted the 2023 CONCACAF Gold Cup Final (Mexico 1-0 Panama), one 2024 Copa America Group D match (Brazil 0-0 Costa Rica), and one 2024 Copa America Group B match (Venezuela 1-0 Mexico).
Set to host opening and closing ceremonies of the 2028 Summer Olympics.
During the 2026 World Cup it is officially branded 'Los Angeles Stadium' under FIFA's clean-venue/neutral-naming policy.
